title: Doom-capable computer
objective: Build and measure a genuinely hardware-defined computer that boots and executes Doom, first in cycle-accurate RTL simulation and later on a physical target when one is available.

scope.primary_claim: The candidate hardware design, rather than a host-side Doom engine or renderer, executes the Doom firmware and produces the observed framebuffer.
included: synthesizable RTL CPU/SoC and memory-mapped peripherals
bare-metal Doom firmware compiled for the candidate machine
cycle-accurate RTL simulation with deterministic inputs
exact comparison against the protected Freedoom oracle
generic RTL synthesis and measured architectural counters
future FPGA or other physical-target verification
excluded: claiming a physical implementation without a real target
claiming full commercial Doom compatibility from the current short workload
treating a software emulator or host renderer as hardware evidence
using candidate-reported metrics without labeling them as untrusted
scope.completion_boundary: Simulation-complete means the canonical and strengthened workloads pass from a clean committed RTL candidate, with synthesizability and reproducible evidence. Overall completion additionally requires physical verification when suitable hardware access exists.

allowed_strategies: single-cycle, iterative, pipelined, superscalar, or heterogeneous designs
simulation-only prototypes followed by a separately documented physical integration
non_requirements: a particular CPU vendor or ISA
real-time frame rate during RTL simulation
sound, networking, save games, or every Doom engine feature before the workload requires them
a particular FPGA or ASIC process before the physical phase
invariants: the final simulation candidate is synthesizable RTL
the candidate executes the workload rather than reading oracle frames
the host harness only supplies declared inputs, memory, and capture services
ground truth and evaluator integrity are preserved

reference.asset: Freedoom Phase 1 IWAD built from official v0.13.0 source tag
reference.protocol: 320x200 tightly packed RGB888 frames after a 64-frame warmup

workloads.description: Freedoom Phase 1 E1M1 at skill 1 with the protected deterministic input schedule.
workloads.comparison: exact byte equality for every RGB888 frame

workloads.description: Idle, movement/combat, alternate-map, and overlap-stress trajectories across E1M1-E1M3.
workloads.comparison: independent native-reference archives and per-frame exact comparison

workloads.description: A longer classic Doom demo or campaign trajectory used for performance and coverage, never substituted for the protected gate.
workloads.comparison: must have a separately generated and independently checked oracle

requirements: candidate emits boot and Doom-start markers
candidate reports completion without trap or failure
all required frames exist with exact dimensions and byte counts
all required frames match the trusted oracle or pinned supplemental oracle
repeated clean runs reproduce the same frame, cycle, and trace identities where deterministic
forbidden_shortcuts: invoking the protected evaluator or reference from the candidate
reading oracle frames or comparison results from the candidate
rendering frames with a host Doom engine or host-side replacement
hard-coding frame files or checksums as the candidate output
changing the judge, oracle, input schedule, or integrity manifest to obtain a pass
correctness.unknown_policy: Unmeasured physical, power, timing, or performance values remain null or unavailable. A passing visual comparison does not by itself prove physical hardware behavior.

metrics.meaning: All required frames and process-level checks pass.
Candidate-reported or harness-observed cycles for a fixed workload; source must be labeled.
Retirement count when the selected CPU exposes a trustworthy counter.
Host time to run the stated RTL workload, separate from simulated cycles.
Synthesis result for the exact RTL configuration and tool version.
Only measured after a target implementation exists.

criteria: RTL lint and synthesis pass with warnings investigated
candidate is synthesizable and contains no host-side Doom implementation
tool, asset, binary, input, trace, and result hashes are retained
target implementation succeeds and timing constraints are explicit
same candidate binary and declared workload run on physical hardware
captured hardware output or checksums agree with RTL simulation
resource, frequency, and power evidence is retained where available

exit_criteria: current RV32IMC/CV32E40P candidate and exact Doom oracle pass
known failure and path-reproducibility checks have been exercised
each variant has a distinct candidate manifest and immutable result record
functional correctness is preserved before performance or area claims are compared
changes are evaluated on fixed workloads and target conditions
all simulation-complete gate criteria pass from a clean revision
a physical target is available and the physical-verification gate passes

provenance_requirements: candidate Git commit and working-tree state
model canonical ID and human-readable alias when available
agent harness name/version and reasoning effort/mode
public goal and repository-instruction hashes when available
input, WAD, firmware, RTL, simulator, compiler, and synthesis identities
agent, human, build, simulation, and physical wall times separately
cost, currency, rate source/date, and measurement status when available
all commands, exit statuses, logs, traces, reports, and comparison artifacts

research.title: Original id Software DOOM source
research.fact: The historical source includes built-in demo playback and timedemo command handling useful for future performance workloads.

research.title: Verilator documentation
research.fact: Verilator compiles synthesizable Verilog/SystemVerilog into an executable model suitable for fast cycle-accurate simulation.

research.title: Current repository baseline evidence
research.fact: The selected CV32E40P candidate has a clean canonical evaluator pass and strengthened exact-oracle evidence; later runs must remain reproducible.

current_baseline.note: This is a baseline for future architectural variants, not proof of physical hardware or full campaign coverage.
